procedural_matters: FRA 1126 was represented by Hind Gaigi.
DEN 1185 was represented by Frederik Hvalsoe.
Prior to the hearing, an arbitration meeting was held; Bence Böröcz (chair of the international jury) acted as arbitrator.
FRA 1126 did not ask to withdraw the protest after the arbitration meeting and neither boat took a Post-Race Penalty under RRS T1(a).
Rasmussen Jeppe Bo (crew of DEN 1185) attended the hearing as an observer.
The panel of the international jury provided tracking evidence.
The panel of the international jury was composed in accordance with RRS N1.4(b).
facts: The conditions at the time of the incident were approximately 10-12 knots of wind and choppy sea.
On the first upwind, FRA 1126 was sailing on a close-hauled course on starboard tack and DEN 1185 on a close- hauled course on port tack, on converging courses.
When the boats were 1 boat length apart, DEN 1185 started to luff to head to wind.
When the boats were half a boat length apart, FRA 1126 luffed by about 10 degrees.
Immediately after, DEN 1185 passed head to wind and bore away to a starboard close-hauled course.
The minimum distance between the boats was 1 meter.
conclusions: There was reasonable doubt that DEN 1185 would have kept clear, if FRA 1126 had not taken avoiding action (see WS Case 50).
DEN 1185 on port tack failed to keep clear of FRA 1126 on starboard tack, and broke RRS 10.
